# Skerry Apiary Handbook

## Spring management

- Open the Skerry hives for the first full inspection when the willow is in catkin and the afternoon air has stayed above 14 degrees for three days running. A brood nest chilled by an early inspection is slow to recover, so the inspection is done between noon and three, with the smoker lit, and the lid is set down upside-down beside the stand so the bees on it can walk back in on their own.
- Queens are marked by the year's colour and clipped only in the apiary's two nucleus yards, never in the home yard where the visitors are shown the hives. A queen that is missing at the first inspection is replaced from a nucleus within 48 hours, because a colony queenless for longer than that begins to produce laying workers that are almost impossible to cure in the spring.
- Feed 2:1 syrup in spring and 1:1 in autumn, and only when the hive is light by the heft test. A frame of stores weighs about two kilograms, and a hive that lifts like an empty box is fed at once, in the evening, with the entrances reduced so that robbing does not start in the neighbouring hives while the feeders are open.
- Swarm control begins when the first queen cells are capped, and the apiary uses the artificial swarm method with the old queen moved to a new floor beside the original stand. Cells are counted at every inspection and the count is written on the lid with chalk, so the next person sees at once how far the colony has gone toward swarming.
- Supers go on when the colony covers eight frames in the brood box, and the queen excluder goes between them only after the first super is half drawn. Honey is taken off by the end of August at the latest, which leaves the colonies six weeks to fill the brood box with winter stores before the ivy flow ends.
